analysis.investment_thesis: Devyani operates KFC, Pizza Hut, and Costa Coffee outlets — a consumer-facing business I would normally examine closely — but the financial structure makes it uninvestable: Debt/Equity of 1.71 (nearly 3.5x my hard limit), persistent net losses (INR -10 Cr in FY24, -7 Cr in FY25), and borrowings that have nearly tripled from INR 1,254 Cr to INR 3,343 Cr in three years. Aggressive expansion funded by debt with no bottom-line profit is the antithesis of how I build wealth.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 61.37% under RJ Corp — strong promoter skin-in-the-game is the one genuine positive
Revenue CAGR of 19.3% over 9 years and consistent OCF generation (INR 900 Cr in FY25) show underlying store-level demand
Gross margin of 50.79% suggests brand-level pricing power at the product level
key_risks: Debt/Equity of 1.71 is catastrophically high by my standards — borrowings of INR 3,343 Cr against equity of INR 1,553 Cr
Finance costs surged from INR 129 Cr to INR 267 Cr (FY22-FY25) and are consuming all operating profit, leaving net losses
Forward P/E of 127.2x for a loss-making QSR franchise operator is pricing in perfection the business has never demonstrated
red_flags: D/E of 1.71 is an explicit dealbreaker — I do not own heavily leveraged consumer businesses at any price
Net profit has been negative in 7 of 10 years tracked; the two profitable years (FY22: INR 155 Cr, FY23: INR 263 Cr) proved unsustainable
Investing CF of -INR 1,551 Cr in FY24 followed by borrowing surge — capital being deployed faster than it earns returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The QSR franchise model is actually one I respect — predictable footfall, brand loyalty, recurring revenue from food. The problem here is entirely structural: Devyani has chosen to grow its store count at maximum speed, financed by debt, before the existing base has proven it can generate sustainable returns. The result is that EBITDA grows (INR 853 Cr in FY25) but finance costs (INR 267 Cr) and lease costs consume it entirely, leaving net losses. Positive OCF is partly a function of IND AS 116 lease accounting.

I built DMart without a single rupee of unnecessary debt and opened each store only when the previous ones proved their payback. Devyani's approach is the opposite — scale first, profitability later. Perhaps that works out, but it is not a bet I will place with my capital. At 1.71x D/E and a forward P/E of 127x with no real earnings, there is no margin of safety. A good business model deserves a cleaner balance sheet before it earns my attention.
